channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: MG: especialistas apontam irregularidade em doação de bens de palácio
item.description: Experts indicate possible irregularities in the donation of 63 decorative furniture items from the Palácio das Mangabeiras to the State General Secretariat, without specifying which objects were transferred, raising suspicions about the disappearance of historical assets. The opposition has appealed to the TCE-MG and Federal Police, citing potential crimes against public property involving Romeu Zema and Mateus Simões. The government claims all assets were inventoried and internally redistributed, but an ALMG inspection found missing books, furniture, paintings, and historical objects.

item.title: Após operação da PF, governo de SP suspende consignados do Digimais
item.description: São Paulo's government, led by Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), temporarily suspended Banco Digimais' authorization to offer payroll-deductible loans to state servants, days after a Federal Police operation (Operation Miragem) seized up to R$670 million in assets and broke banking and fiscal secrecy of the bank's owners. The suspension relies on 'extreme urgency' legislation, despite the same digital government secretary having authorized Digimais in June 2025 — including for military police, granting access to over 80,000 agents. The move draws opposition criticism over alleged institutional favoritism due to ties between the Universal Church, Digimais, and the Republicanos party.

item.title: Como sobrevivem os partidos que não recebem Fundo Partidário: doações, filiados e outras receitas bancam gastos
item.description: Nine Brazilian parties survive almost without the Party Fund, relying on donations, member contributions and other revenues to finance their activities. DC was the highest earner among them, with R$ 2.8 million in 2025, nearly all from individual donations, while Mobiliza and PRTB spent more than they raised. PSTU relied primarily on member contributions, which accounted for 75% of its revenue.

item.title: Presidente do TSE reúne institutos de pesquisa para tratar de critérios de levantamentos eleitorais nesta terça-feira
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques is meeting with electoral research institutes on Tuesday to discuss criteria for conducting and publishing voter intention polls, aiming to prevent data contamination and judicial disputes. The meeting follows the May suspension of an AtlasIntel poll and seeks to establish guidelines on technology, verbal neutrality, and digital research flow, with most institutes represented by a lawyer from ABEP.

item.title: Governo tenta acordo para votar MP do frete para superar pressão dos caminhoneiros: veja pontos em negociação
item.description: The Lula government is negotiating in the Senate to approve a provisional measure that would expand ANTT's powers to monitor and punish violations of the minimum freight table, which risks expiring if not voted this week. Talks focus on the minimum freight floor and the CIOT tracking system, though the government has ruled out setting a specific value in the text, citing STF jurisprudence that bars Congress from establishing floors in infraconstitutional laws. The MP aims to ease diesel price impacts on truckers by maintaining a calculation methodology based on distance, vehicle type, cargo, and input costs.

item.title: Às vésperas de tarifaço, governo Lula trabalha com duas hipóteses para decisão de Trump: veja quais
item.description: The Lula government is preparing two scenarios for the impending U.S. decision on a new tariff on Brazilian products, expected within 24 hours. The strategy involves either escalating tariffs or maintaining the status quo, aiming to minimize economic damage.

item.title: Os efeitos da decisão de Alexandre de Moraes na guerra entre Michelle e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The decision by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to prohibit Senator Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting former President Jair Bolsonaro provoked outrage among allies and highlighted divergent interpretations of its impact on both Flávio and Michelle Bolsonaro. The ruling positions Michelle as the main interlocutor with Jair at a pivotal moment in the family feud, as the electoral calendar advances and state-level slates and party conventions are being defined.

item.title: Presidente eleito da Colômbia contraria Petro e diz que tomará posse em base militar
item.description: Colombia's president-elect, Abelardo De la Espriella, announced he will take office in August at a military base in the country's south, defying an order from outgoing President Gustavo Petro, who banned the use of military installations for the ceremony. De la Espriella stated the act is a tribute to the military and the Constitution, and has requested authorization from the incoming Congress, which convenes on July 20, to hold a modest inauguration. Petro maintains that the armed forces remain under his command until the inauguration and that no officer should salute a civilian who is not their supreme commander.

item.title: URGENTE: Flávio Bolsonaro fala de possivel INTERFERÊNCIA NAS ELEIÇÕES 2026
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro warned of potential interference in the 2026 elections, suggesting that external or institutional forces might attempt to manipulate the outcome. He made these remarks amid rising political polarization in Brazil, reinforcing narratives of distrust in the electoral system. The senator provided no concrete evidence but linked his concerns to recent incidents of disinformation and pressure on democratic institutions.

item.title: Imposto sobre dividendos arrecada só 5% do previsto para o ano e pode frustrar projeção do governo
item.description: The federal government collected only R$1.54 billion from the Income Tax on dividends through May, equivalent to 5.13% of the R$29.9 billion annual revenue target set by the economic team. This underperformance risks undermining the government's fiscal projections and may prompt revisions to budgetary forecasts.

item.title: Governo Lula não vê espaço para acordo com EUA sobre tarifas e rejeita negociar Pix e etanol
item.description: The Lula government says there is no room for an agreement with the United States on the new tariff round before next Wednesday (15), when the U.S. is expected to announce its decision on implementing the measure. The government also rejected negotiating issues such as Pix and ethanol in trade talks.

item.title: Lula comentou Copa na prisão, manteve perfis em redes e não tinha restrição para divulgar cartas
item.description: Former President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) commented on the 2018 World Cup while imprisoned in 2018, maintained active social media profiles, and faced no restrictions on publishing letters during his incarceration. This contrasts with the severe communication restrictions imposed on former President Jair Bolsonaro (PL) during his current house arrest in 2026.

item.title: Pesquisa: o movimento que pode indicar que eleitores de Lula e Flávio estão repensando voto
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows stability in the presidential race between Lula (40%) and Flávio Bolsonaro (34%) in the first round, with a technical tie in the second round (47% to 40%). Despite overall stability, there was a notable shift in spontaneous voting: Lula dropped from 38% to 35% and Flávio from 27% to 24%, with the six-point loss split among blank/null votes, undecided voters, and third-way candidates, suggesting possible voter reconsideration among supporters of the two main candidates.

item.title: Janja diz que não será candidata e quer “vida de mulher casada”
item.description: First Lady Rosângela da Silva, known as Janja, stated she does not intend to run for any office and wishes to live a private life as a married woman after Lula’s current political cycle ends. She reiterated her support for Lula’s re-election in 2026 and said the PT must develop new leadership without her specifying names. Janja also defended her government role, emphasizing her work on policies against femicide, food security, and protection of women and children.

item.title: Xandão violou a advocacia? Ora, botemos um pouco de ordem nessa orgia!
item.description: The text criticizes lawyer Tracy Reinaldet's claim that the contact ban between Flávio and Jair Bolsonaro violates attorney-client rights, arguing such rights are not absolute and can be restricted, as seen in high-security prisons for PCC and CV leaders. It also dismisses Senator Rogério Marinho's incorrect statement against Alexandre de Moraes' decision, linking it to far-right aspirations for political praise. The author invokes a provocative metaphor from the Marquis de Sade to advocate for ordering the debate, avoiding both excessive explicitness and vulgarity.

item.title: Os novos segredos de Flávio Bolsonaro e o ‘festival de indiretas’ de aliados de Michelle
item.description: The struggle for Jair Bolsonaro’s political legacy is intensifying, with allies of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro expecting damaging revelations to surface, while Michelle Bolsonaro’s allies escalate indirect attacks, exemplified by Senator Damares Alves praising Michelle without mentioning Flávio. Jair Bolsonaro’s public reaffirmation of support for Flávio—without acknowledging Michelle—was seen as a misstep that worsened the family and political rift within the bolsonarist movement.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio calcula prejuízos com proibição de visitas e vê impacto em estratégias
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) pre-campaign team plans to appeal to the STF to overturn Justice Alexandre de Moraes' decision banning contact, until after the first round of the 2026 elections, between the senator and his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro (PL), who is under house arrest. The campaign views the restriction as damaging to its electoral strategy.

item.title: Janja presta solidariedade a Michelle Bolsonaro e Damares Alves
item.description: First Lady Janja Silva expressed solidarity with Michelle Bolsonaro and Damares Alves, who were targeted in a dispute with Flávio Bolsonaro, stating that violence against women has no ideological side. She emphasized the urgency of passing the Misogyny Bill and denounced being a target of misogyny through the 'Janjômeter', calling it part of the far-right's strategy to reach President Lula. Janja also denied the need for a formal position for her role in the Planalto.

item.title: Moraes é o marqueteiro do Flávio, ironiza Renan Santos
item.description: Renan Santos, pre-candidate for presidency from the Missão party, accused Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes of acting as a 'marketer' for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro by suspending Flávio's right to visit his father, Jair Bolsonaro, under house arrest, for 90 days. Renan claimed the decision politically benefits the Bolsonaro clan, indicating STF partiality. The statement was made in an interview with O Antagonista.

item.title: O grande ‘cabo eleitoral’ que Alexandre de Moraes deu a Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The 90-day ban on visits by Alexandre de Moraes to former President Jair Bolsonaro strengthens the bolsonarist narrative of persecution, according to columnist Robson Bonin. The measure is seen as a key electoral asset for Flávio Bolsonaro, who aims to position himself as the main voice of the right and leverage the Supreme Court confrontation as a mobilizing tool in the 2026 campaign.

item.title: Eduardo defende que EUA restabeleçam a Magnitsky contra Moraes
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro urged the United States to reinstate the Magnitsky Act against Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, following Moraes' 90-day suspension of visits from Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to former President Jair Bolsonaro, which Eduardo labeled as abusive.

item.title: Renan Santos chama Moraes de 'cabo eleitoral' de Flávio por suspender visitas a Bolsonaro
item.description: Presidential candidate Renan Santos of the Missão party accused Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes of acting as a 'campaign aide' for Flávio Bolsonaro by suspending the senator’s 90-day visits to imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro, claiming the decision fuels a persecution narrative and boosts Flávio’s candidacy. The ruling, tied to the release of a letter from Jair Bolsonaro supporting his son, also refers the case to the electoral prosecutor for investigation of potential premature campaigning. Jair Bolsonaro is under house arrest after being convicted of leading a coup plot.

item.title: “Eu fui assediada como primeira-dama”, diz Janja
item.description: First Lady Janja revealed she was sexually harassed twice while in office during public events with President Lula, and chose to speak out to raise awareness and show that no woman is safe, regardless of position. She immediately supported former Minister Anielle Franco, who accused then-Minister Silvio Almeida of sexual harassment, criticizing the excessive burden placed on victims. Janja emphasized her role in combating gender-based violence, including her leadership in the National Pact Against Femicide.

item.title: Carlos Bolsonaro diz que ‘militarização’ foi um dos maiores erros do governo do pai
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro (PL-SC) criticized the 'militarization' of his father Jair Bolsonaro's government, calling it one of the biggest mistakes due to lack of political structure. He stated that his brother Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) will not repeat this model, favoring technically qualified personnel. Ipea data shows military presence in civilian federal posts nearly tripled from 2013 to 2021, with sharp increases in Economy, Health, and Environment ministries.

item.title: Janja diz ser alvo de misoginia e que críticas sobre gastos em viagens são para atacar Lula
item.description: First Lady Janja da Silva said she is a target of misogyny and that criticism over her travel expenses is part of a far-right strategy to attack President Lula. She denied needing an official position to carry out her duties, emphasized that her activities are public and transparent, and called the Janjômeter website misleading and exaggerated, as verified by Estadão Verifica.

item.title: Janja presta solidariedade a Michelle e Damares após ataques: 'Não pode soltar a mão, não importa qual campo ideológico'
item.description: First Lady Janja Lula da Silva expressed solidarity with Michelle Bolsonaro and Damares Alves following attacks against them, including death threats against Damares' daughter. Janja stressed that defending women must transcend ideological divides, stating misogyny has no political side and advocating for the approval of the misogyny criminalization bill in the Chamber of Deputies.

item.title: Janja descarta que cargo formal seja solução para sua atuação
item.description: First Lady Janja stated she does not see holding a formal government position as necessary for her role, emphasizing that her work is already regulated for transparency. She explained she maintains a regular work routine at the Palácio do Planalto, attending meetings, trips, and inter-ministerial articulations, with her agenda publicly disclosed daily. Janja also noted that media coverage often focuses on her personal life and international travels rather than her institutional activities.

item.title: Se direita vencer eleição, haverá interrupção democrática, diz ministro
item.description: The Minister of Entrepreneurship, Paulo Henrique Pereira, warned that a right-wing victory in the 2026 presidential elections could trigger a 'wave of democratic interruption' affecting an entire generation. He emphasized the importance of the alliance with the PT to counter what he described as an still-active and dangerous far-right, noting that Brazil narrowly escaped a coup and cannot afford to repeat the risk.

item.title: 'Bolsonaro é quem vai colocar a faixa de presidente em mim', diz Flávio sobre a possibilidade de vencer as eleições
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, PL pre-candidate for president, stated in a live broadcast that if he wins the October 2026 election, his father, Jair Bolsonaro, will place the presidential sash on him during the January 2027 inauguration, despite the former president serving house arrest for attempting a coup. Flávio expressed confidence that his father’s legal situation will be reversed and pledged to 'rescue Brazil,' criticizing Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes for restricting his visits to his father after a letter of support was shared on social media.

item.title: Janja presta solidariedade a Damares e Michelle Bolsonaro após ataques: ‘Não importa o campo ideológico’
item.description: First Lady Janja da Silva expressed solidarity with Senator Damares Alves and former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro following misogynistic attacks, stating that political violence against women has no ideological boundary. She emphasized that misogyny affects all women equally, regardless of political alignment, during an interview on UOL’s Frente a Frente program.

item.title: Eleições 2026: PT vê recuperação de Flávio Bolsonaro entre jovens e evangélicos | CNN PRIME TIME
item.description: The PT observes that Flávio Bolsonaro, senator and son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, is gaining support among young people and evangelical voters, suggesting a potential recovery of his political capital ahead of the 2026 elections. This trend is viewed with concern by the party, which is trying to understand the reasons behind his rising popularity in sectors traditionally aligned with the right. CNN Prime Time highlights that this shift in voter profile could impact the PT’s campaign strategies in 2026.

item.title: Rede pede a Fachin que suspenda mudança de prazo da Lei da Ficha Limpa
item.description: The Rede Sustentabilidade party has requested that STF President Minister Luiz Edson Fachin grant an injunction to suspend the effects of Complementary Law 219 of 2025, which changes the calculation of the Ficha Limpa ineligibility period to start from the date of conviction rather than the completion of the sentence. The party argues urgency due to the approaching 2026 party conventions and the recess of rapporteur Minister Cármen Lúcia, who has already voted to declare the law unconstitutional, calling it a blatant setback for administrative morality.

item.title: Janja diz que apelido de “gastadeira” é “misoginia pura”
item.description: First Lady Rosângela Lula da Silva, known as Janja, stated that the nickname 'gastadeira' used against her is a pure example of misogyny, explaining that she travels in executive class for security reasons mandated by the Federal Police, not personal choice. She emphasized her active role in the Presidency, attending meetings, undertaking official trips, and maintaining a public agenda, noting that this model of engagement still causes surprise in Brazilian society. Janja also urged the approval of a bill to criminalize misogyny, currently stalled in the Chamber of Deputees, and noted that the TCU unanimously archived four processes regarding her international travel expenses since 2023, finding no evidence of misuse of public funds.

item.title: Flávio pede que OAB se manifeste após Moraes suspender visitas a Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) called on the Brazilian Bar Association (OAB) to take a stance after Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes suspended, for 90 days, the right to visit former President Jair Bolsonaro, following Flávio’s public reading of a letter from his father, which violated a court order banning third-party social media use. Flávio, who formally joined Bolsonaro’s legal defense team in March, argues the suspension infringes on his constitutional right as a lawyer to communicate with his client, even if he is the senator’s son. The measure was imposed because Bolsonaro is under house arrest and prohibited from using social media, including through intermediaries.

item.title: Zema cobra fim de politicagem em post da CBF
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) criticized the Brazilian Football Confederation's (CBF) post honoring the national team after its World Cup elimination, accusing it of politicization. Zema argued the post strayed from sports into political territory, which he deemed inappropriate. He urged sports institutions to remain neutral and focus solely on athletic matters.

item.title: Lula acusa EUA de "pirataria" por anunciar que cobrará taxa em Ormuz
item.description: President Lula accused the United States of becoming a 'pirate' nation if it imposes fees on ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, as announced by Donald Trump. The statement was made on Monday (13) and reflects growing tensions in trade and maritime navigation between the two countries.

item.title: Renan Santos chama Moraes de 'marqueteiro' e 'cabo eleitoral' de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Renan Santos, a pre-candidate for president from the Missão party, criticized the decision by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to prohibit Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting former president Jair Bolsonaro, calling the justice a 'political marketer' and 'campaign operative' for Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Lula diz que não vai ter tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: President Lula stated that there will be no US tariff hike on Brazilian products, despite expectations of new tariffs up to 25% on Brazilian exports, linked to a USTR investigation into alleged illegal trade practices, including Pix. The comment was made after his visit to the first ethanol-powered turbine project (UGEE1000BR) in São José dos Campos, developed by IAE/DCTA, attended by officials including Alckmin, Silveira, Boulos, Mercadante, and Marina Silva.

item.title: Por que Lula pôde divulgar cartas quando estava preso? ex-advogado de petista responde
item.description: Lula's former lawyer, Manoel Caetano Ferreira, states that Lula's disclosure of letters while imprisoned in 2018-2019 was lawful because no judicial restriction barred his communication, unlike Bolsonaro's current situation, which involves violating precautionary measures. The comparison between the two cases is legally unfounded, as Lula was not subject to any communication ban. Lula's 2018 letter endorsed Fernando Haddad, while Bolsonaro's 2026 letter supported Flávio Bolsonaro, prompting Moraes to prohibit visits.

item.title: Lula critica atuação dos EUA no Estreito de Ormuz e classifica cobranças como ‘pirataria’
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva strongly criticized recent U.S. proposals to impose fees on maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, labeling them as acts of 'piracy'. He emphasized that the Strait of Hormuz is a critical artery for global energy trade, through which about one-fifth of the world's consumed oil passes, and warned that such measures undermine free navigation and international stability.

item.title: A resposta pública de Flávio à decisão de Moraes sobre visita a Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro accused Justice Alexandre de Moraes of attempting to interfere in the 2026 elections by banning, for 90 days, visits from his father, Jair Bolsonaro, under house arrest, following the public disclosure of a letter by the former president. Flávio called the move an effort to isolate his father and suggested the timing was deliberate to harm his electoral prospects. Moraes defended the decision, stating that sharing the letter on social media violated house arrest rules and could constitute premature electoral propaganda.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro diz que lei Magnitsky contra Moraes deve ser restabelecida
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro urged the reinstatement of the U.S. Magnitsky Act against Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, arguing that the suspension of visits from Flávio Bolsonaro to his father, Jair Bolsonaro, constitutes political abuse and undermines the democratic legitimacy of the 2026 elections. The sanctions, previously applied in 2023 and lifted in December, targeted Moraes and his wife over alleged human rights abuses. Eduardo, residing in the U.S. and facing charges in Brazil for attempting to obstruct his father’s trial, is lobbying the Trump administration to reimpose the measures.

item.title: Renan Santos chama Moraes de ‘marqueteiro’ e ‘cabo eleitoral’ de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Renan Santos, a pré-candidate for President from the Mission party, criticized Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to ban Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting Jair Bolsonaro, arguing it strengthens bolsonarism by fostering a persecution narrative. He compared it to Lula's support for Haddad in 2018 and claimed Moraes acts as Flávio Bolsonaro's 'electoral cabo' and 'marketer', diverting attention from scandals like the Banco Master case.

item.title: Lula diz não acreditar que haverá novo tarifaço dos EUA contra o Brasil
item.description: President Lula stated he does not believe the United States will impose a new 25% tariff on Brazilian products, despite the USTR’s recommendation to apply the surcharge due to trade imbalances linked to digital trade, Pix, intellectual property, and deforestation. The final decision rests with President Donald Trump and is expected by July 15. Lula made the remark at an event in São José dos Campos, two days before the USTR’s final recommendation.

item.title: “Você, enquanto juíza, dando opiniões num regime. O que queria? Flores?”
item.description: Former federal deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL) criticized former judge Ludmila Lins Grilo after she questioned the pre-campaign strategy of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) to disseminate a letter from former President Jair Bolsonaro (PL), who is under house arrest. Eduardo accused the judge of acting with partisanship in an authoritarian regime, using irony by asking if she 'wanted flowers' instead of allowing the former president's communication. The incident highlights tensions between Bolsonaro's circle and the judiciary.

item.title: Janja: o Brasil nunca teve uma primeira-dama que trabalhasse efetivamente
item.description: First Lady Rosângela da Silva, known as Janja, defended her active role in the Lula government, stating that Brazil has never had a first lady who worked effectively. She attributed criticism to society and the press not being accustomed to the presidential spouse’s active participation, citing class prejudice as a underlying factor. Janja emphasized her daily work schedule, official agendas, international trips, and initiatives against hunger and menstrual poverty, while dismissing cost-related accusations as misogynistic.

item.title: Janja diz que críticas sobre gastos no exterior são 'misoginia' e afirma ser a única primeira-dama do Brasil que 'trabalha efetivamente'
item.description: First Lady Janja Lula da Silva defended her international travels and government work, labeling criticisms of being a 'spendthrift' as misogyny and class prejudice. She stated she is Brazil's first first lady to work 'effectively,' with an office at the Planalto Palace and a daily public agenda, and compared her trajectory to that of Ruth Cardoso, emphasizing her humble origins and public university education.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro: "Magnitsky contra Moraes deve ser restabelecida"
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro criticized Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to suspend visits from Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro, proposing the application of the Magnitsky Act against Moraes. He argued that banning communication between a jailed presidential candidate and his son constitutes political interference and undermines the democratic legitimacy of the 2026 elections. The STF's measure followed the dissemination of a letter from Jair Bolsonaro supporting Flávio's candidacy, which violated a judicial order prohibiting the ex-president from using social media directly or through intermediaries.

item.title: Pesquisa BTG/Nexus: Desejo por terceira via dispara para 27%
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows that preference for a third-way candidate in the 2026 Brazilian elections rose from 11% in March to 27% in July, reflecting growing dissatisfaction with options tied to Lula and Bolsonaro. Although the first round is not yet defined, this significant increase suggests a potential reconfiguration of Brazil's electoral landscape.

item.title: Zema cita 'farra suja' em post da CBF após eliminação do Brasil na Copa: 'Comecem acabando com essa politicagem'
item.description: Romeu Zema, a presidential pre-candidate and former governor of Minas Gerais, criticized the CBF in comments on an institutional video, accusing the organization of prioritizing accountability to Brasília over Brazilian fans and of being subjected to 'politicagem' and 'dirty dealing'. He reiterated claims that Francisco Mendes, son of Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes, exerts undue influence over the CBF, citing an alleged agreement between the IDP (linked to Mendes' family) and the CBF, and influence on Neymar's call-up. Zema linked these allegations to a 2024 decision by Gilmar Mendes that restored the CBF's leadership.
